title: Series-Parallel 2: A Line Resistor and a Nested Branch
description: A 48 V source feeds R1 (4 Ω) in series with a parallel group: one branch is R2 (6 Ω) and R3 (6 Ω) in series, the other branch is R4 (12 Ω). Two levels of reduction are needed.

tasks.question: What is the total resistance of the circuit?
What is the total current from the 48 V source?
What is the voltage across R1 (the line resistor)?
What is the voltage across R3?
What total power does the source deliver?

hints: Work from the inside out. R2 and R3 are in series with each other: combine them first (6 + 6 = 12 Ω).
That 12 Ω branch is in parallel with R4 (12 Ω): two equal resistors in parallel give half, 6 Ω.
Now the circuit is R1 (4 Ω) in series with 6 Ω. R_total = 10 Ω and I_total = 48 ÷ 10.
V_R1 = I_total × 4. The parallel group gets the rest. The two 12 Ω branches split the group current equally, and inside the R2-R3 branch that branch current flows through both resistors.
Check: the power in all four resistors should add to V_source × I_total.
learningGoals: Reduce a circuit with series elements nested inside a parallel group.
Track which voltage applies to each level of the circuit.
Use power conservation as a final check.
disclaimer: Simulated bench exercise; not field experience.
